explanation: Mathlib has no `IsLocallyNormalRing` (or any `IsNormal` for schemes/rings): grepping Mathlib for `IsLocallyNormalRing` and case-insensitive `locally normal` yields nothing relevant (`IsNormal` occurs only for order/ordinal functions and subgroupoids). The theorem's content is descent of the library's own class `IsLocallyNormalRing` (all prime localizations are integrally closed domains) along a faithfully flat algebra, and Mathlib contains no declaration stating that integral closedness, nor the conjunction 'domain + integrally closed', descends along flat/faithfully flat maps (searches for `IsIntegrallyClosed` combined with `Flat`/`FaithfullyFlat`, and for `IsDomain` descent, only give `IsDomain.of_faithfulSMul` and localization-based results, which are much weaker). The proof merely uses Mathlib ingredients (e.g. `PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat`, `Ideal.comap_map_eq_self_of_faithfullyFlat`, `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom`, `isIntegrallyClosed_iff`) and combines them in a substantial argument, so no single Mathlib declaration yields this result.
